overclaims: The core of the claim is that Operator could not control a computer consistently and was not ready for general use.
On full computer-control tasks it succeeded 38.1% of the time, against 72.4% for humans (e2).
Early independent testers found it made too many mistakes to rely on without constant supervision (e3).
checks.note: The rationale strengthens 'does not appear able' to 'could not'. It attributes CUA's OSWorld benchmark result to Operator without distinguishing the model from the product. It also drops 'for important tasks' from The Decoder's supervision finding. Preserve those qualifications and identify CUA explicitly. The excerpt, proposition, target period, citations, and agreed outcome otherwise match.
